extraction.name: DocVQA
extraction.description: DocVQA is a large-scale dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images. It consists of 50,000 questions defined on 12,767 document images sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library. The documents span many decades (1900-2018) and cover five major industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, chemical) with a wide variety of document types including letters, forms, reports, tables, and figures. Questions require models to not only read text but also interpret it within the layout/structure of the document.
extraction.creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
extraction.publisher: CVIT, IIIT Hyderabad; Computer Vision Center, UAB
extraction.citeAs: Mathew, M., Karatzas, D., & Jawahar, C.V. (2021). DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images. arXiv:2007.00398v3
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library. Documents were downloaded from different collections and pages were hand-picked for use in the dataset. The authors prioritized non-binarized images and pages with tables, forms, lists and figures over pages with only running text. Questions and answers were collected with the help of remote workers using a Web based annotation tool through a three-stage annotation process.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images sourced from UCSF Industry Documents Library (https://www.industrydocuments.ucsf.edu/), covering documents from 5 major industries: tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, and chemical. 6,071 industry documents were used.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors tried to minimize binarized images in DocVQA since poor image quality would be a bottleneck for VQA. Pages with tables, forms, lists and figures were prioritized over pages with only running text. For BERT QA experiments, OCR tokens were serialized to a single string separated by space in top-left to bottom-right order. The data was split randomly in an 80-10-10 ratio to train, validation and test splits.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three-stage annotation process: Stage 1 (Question Answer Collection): workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs, encouraged to add more than one ground truth answer when warranted, and instructed to ask questions answerable using text present in the image, entering answers verbatim. Stage 2 (Data Verification): a different worker was shown an image and questions from stage 1 (without seeing the answers) and was required to enter answers and assign one or more question types to each question. Workers could flag inapt questions. Stage 3 (Review): if none of the stage 1 answers matched exactly with any stage 2 answers, the question was sent for review by the authors who could edit or ignore it.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions sent for third-stage review were those where none of the answers entered in the first stage matched exactly with any answers from the second stage. In the third stage, authors reviewed, edited if necessary, and either accepted or ignored questions. Annotators could also flag questions due to language issues or ambiguity.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Multiple ground truth answers per question were encouraged when warranted. Questions are tagged with one or more of 9 question types.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Remote workers; annotation effort was supported by Amazon. A few volunteers from the authors' institution provided human performance answers on the test split.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: A commercial OCR application was used to extract OCR tokens from document images.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, code and leaderboard are available at docvqa.org
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Documents contain named entities such as names of people, institutions and places. Top non-numeric answers include names of individuals (e.g., Dr. William J. Darby, Robert E. Shank).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors aim to inspire a 'purpose-driven' approach in document image analysis and recognition research, driving methods that use low-level cues (text, layout, arrangements) and high-level goals (purpose, relationship, domain knowledge) in solving problems of practical importance.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Most of the documents are from the 1960-2000 period. Documents originate from 5 specific industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, chemical), with many documents from food and nutrition related collections because they have more non-binarized images. Top answers are predominantly numeric values because there are a good number of document images of reports and invoices.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Image quality is affected by binarization of many source documents. OCR errors impact model performance. The dataset is extractive in nature—answers are expected to be present as text in the document image. Existing models have a large performance gap compared to human performance (94.36% accuracy), particularly on questions requiring understanding of document structure.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, and Testing for Visual Question Answering on document images. The dataset is designed as an extractive QA problem. Use cases include developing models that simultaneously use visual and textual cues for answering questions on document images, driving DAR algorithms to conditionally interpret document images.
